items.text: I follow steps, one at a time, in order. Your steps get me to the flower.

items.prompt: Tap a step to get me to the flower.
items.explain: One step right and I'm there.

items.prompt: Three steps this time. I start as soon as the last one is in.
items.explain: Right, right, right: three steps along the row.

items.prompt: The flower is up a row. Build the steps.
items.explain: Three steps right and one up. Up first works too: there's more than one way.

items.prompt: This flower is behind me. Two steps.
items.explain: Left, left. I walk whichever way the blocks say.

items.prompt: Now it sits a row below me. Three steps.
items.explain: Two right and one down. Any order that stays on the grid gets there.

items.text: Watch. The steps run out before the flower, so I stop where the last one put me. I never add a step of my own.

items.prompt: Read my steps. Tap the square where I stop.
items.explain: Right, right, then down: two along and one down.

items.prompt: Three steps, one at a time. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Down, right, down: that lands one along and two down, next to the flower.

items.text: Rocks are in the way. I can't walk through them, so the steps go around.

items.prompt: Get me round the rock to the flower.
items.explain: Down, right, right, up: under the rock and back up.

items.prompt: A taller rock. Six steps.
items.explain: Down twice, right twice, up twice: all the way round.

items.prompt: This time the way round is along the top.
items.explain: Up, right, right, down: along the top row and back down.

items.prompt: Rocks in two places. Four steps, and the order matters.
items.explain: Down and right first. After that, down and right in either order both get there.

items.text: Watch. The right step hits the rock, so I stop there. The down step never happens: a rock, or the edge of the grid, ends the run.

items.prompt: A rock is on my way. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: One step right, then the rock blocks the next one, so I stop there. A step into a rock ends the run.

items.prompt: The edge counts as well. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Up is the edge of the grid, so the run ends before I take a single step.

items.prompt: Three steps along a row of three squares. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two steps reach the end of the row. The third hits the edge, so I stop there.

items.text: Longer walks now. Before you tap, find the whole way with your eyes. Then build it from the first step to the last.

items.prompt: Seven steps. Find the way past the rocks first.
items.explain: Down to the bottom row, along past the rocks, then up to the flower.

items.prompt: A tall rock. Eight steps, down one side and back along the other.
items.explain: Three down, two right, three up: all the way round the rock.

items.prompt: Five steps. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two right, two down, one left: that lands one along and two down.

items.prompt: Down through one gap, up through the next. Eight steps.
items.explain: Right, down, down, right, right, up, up, right. The rocks leave one way through.

items.prompt: A long plan with a rock on the row. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two steps right, then the rock blocks the third. The run ends there and the down step never happens.

items.prompt: To reach this flower I go past it and come back.
items.explain: Right three times, up twice, then left twice. Sometimes the way there starts by heading away.

items.prompt: Five steps, and one of them bumps. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Down, right, right, then up is a rock. The run ends there and the last step never happens.

items.prompt: An open field, five steps, many good plans. Pick any.
items.explain: Three right and two down, in any order. Every one of those plans is good.

items.text: Bigger maps, fewer ways through. Same plan as ever: one square at a time, and count before you tap.

items.prompt: One way through. Eight steps.
items.explain: Down, right, right, up, right, right, down, down. The rocks allow only that one.

items.prompt: All the way along, down the far side, and all the way back.
items.explain: Three right, two down, three left. Long plans are small plans in a row.

items.prompt: Six steps. Follow them with your finger, then tap where I stop.
items.explain: Down, three right, up, right: that gets me all the way to the flower.

items.prompt: Only two kinds of step this time. Five steps.
items.explain: Down, right, down, right, right. Fewer tiles, and the order does the work.

items.prompt: Around the rocks and back. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two right, two down, two left: that ends on the flower.

items.prompt: Look at the second step. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The first step down is fine. The second hits the rock, so I stop one square below the start.

items.prompt: The flower is inside the rocks. Find the door.
items.explain: Four right, two down, two left: the only door is on the far side.

items.text: A repeat block does what's inside it again and again. Repeat 4 times → is the same as → → → →, with less tapping.

items.prompt: How many times should I step right?
items.explain: Four squares to the flower, so repeat 4 times.

items.prompt: The count is set. Pick the step to repeat.
items.explain: Right, five times in a row.

items.prompt: Same block, new direction. How many times down?
items.explain: Four squares below me, so repeat 4 times.

items.text: Watch. With two steps inside, I do them in order, then go back to the top and do both again.

items.prompt: Stairs! Two steps inside, done three times.
items.explain: Right then up, three times: a staircase. Up first runs into a rock.

items.prompt: Read the loop. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right and down, two rounds: two along and two down.

items.prompt: Read the count. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Three times right is three squares, one short of the flower. The count decides, not the flower.

items.prompt: A rock on my row. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two steps, then the rock blocks the third. A repeat does not get me past a rock.

items.prompt: A long way. How many times?
items.explain: Six squares, so repeat 6 times. Counting the gaps is the trick.

items.text: Watch. One loop runs to its end, then the next one starts.

items.prompt: One loop goes right, the next goes down. Set both counts.
items.explain: Right 3 times, then down 2 times. One loop finishes before the next one starts.

items.prompt: Now the counts are set. Pick each loop's step.
items.explain: Right 3 times, then down 3 times.

items.prompt: Three loops, one after another. Set each count.
items.explain: Right 3, up 2, left 3. Each loop finishes before the next one starts.

items.prompt: A loop, then one plain step. Fill both.
items.explain: Right 3 times, then one step down. Loops and plain steps mix freely.

items.prompt: A loop, then one more step. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Three steps right, then the loop is done and I step up once.

items.prompt: Two loops. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two down, then three right: the flower stays up on its own row.

items.text: Now you pick both: how many times, and what goes inside. Look for the piece of the path that comes round again.

items.prompt: Fill in the count and the step.
items.explain: Right, 4 times. You chose both parts this time.

items.prompt: The flower is straight above me. Fill in both.
items.explain: Up, 3 times.

items.prompt: Stairs. How many times round, and which two steps?
items.explain: Down then right, 3 times. Right first runs into a rock.

items.prompt: Three steps inside this time. Find the piece that comes round.
items.explain: Right, right, up, 2 times. The second round ends on the flower.

items.prompt: Three steps inside, three rounds. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two rounds carry me to the far column. The third round's first step hits the edge.

items.prompt: Three whole loops to build.
items.explain: Right 3, down 2, left 3. Three short loops instead of eight taps.

items.prompt: Four steps inside. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Up, right, down, then the rock blocks the next step. The run ends there, part-way through the first round.

items.prompt: Stairs the other way. Fill in all three.
items.explain: Up then left, 3 times. Left first runs into a rock.

items.text: Long maps, few blocks. Find the pattern before you tap, and let the count do the walking.

items.prompt: A long staircase. Count the steps of the stairs.
items.explain: Down then right, 4 times.

items.prompt: The counts tell you how far. Pick each step.
items.explain: Down 4, right 2, up 4: three small loops and a long walk.

items.prompt: A very long fence. Set each count.
items.explain: Right 6, down 2, left 6. Count the gaps between squares, not the squares.

items.prompt: A loop, then one more step. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right, right, down, two rounds. Then the last step right, one square further along.

items.prompt: Five rounds on this long row. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Five steps right, and the flower is six away. One count short is a very common slip.

items.prompt: A long loop on a short row. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Three steps, then the rock blocks the fourth. The run ends, so the down step never happens.

items.prompt: Find the piece that comes round, then count it.
items.explain: Right, right, down, 2 times.

items.prompt: Everything is empty. Build the whole walk.
items.explain: Right 5, up 2, left 5.

items.text: An if block looks at the very next square. If there's a rock right beside me on my right, I do the first step. Else, meaning no rock there, I do the other one.
Watch. In a repeat, I look again each time round. Rock beside me, so up. Then no rock, so right, and right again.

items.prompt: Rock to my right: which way? No rock: which way?
items.explain: If a rock is to my right, step up. Else, step right. The same two blocks climb any rocks like these.

items.prompt: Now I'm going down. Rock below me: which way? No rock: which way?
items.explain: If a rock is below me, step right. Else, step down.

items.prompt: Now I'm heading left. Rock to my left: which way? No rock: which way?
items.explain: If a rock is to my left, step up. Else, step left.

items.prompt: Follow the if each time round. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: A rock to my right, so down. Then no rock, so right, and right again.

items.prompt: Two rounds. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: A rock to my right both times, so down and down again. Two rounds, two looks.

items.prompt: No rocks on this row at all. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: No rock either time, so the else runs twice: two steps right.

items.text: One if, one look. With no repeat around it, I look once, do one thing and stop.

items.prompt: One if and no repeat. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: No rock beside me, so one step right. Then the blocks have run out.

items.prompt: The if is ready. How many times round?
items.explain: Right, right, then rocks, so up, up: 4 times round.

items.prompt: Going up. Rock above me: which way? No rock: which way?
items.explain: If a rock is above me, step right. Else, step up.

items.text: Watch. The edge of the grid counts as a rock when I look. At the end of the row I go down.

items.prompt: No rocks on this map, only the edge. Which way for each?
items.explain: The edge counts as a rock. At the end of the row, step down. Else, step right.

items.prompt: The if is ready. How many rounds to reach the flower?
items.explain: Right, down, right, right: 4 rounds.

items.prompt: One last read. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right, then a rock, so down. Then right and right again.

items.text: Now you pick what I look for too. The first gap in an if is the direction I check. Look for the rock that matters.

items.prompt: Which way should I look?
items.explain: Look right. The rock beside me is the one that sends me up.

items.prompt: I'm going down. Which way should I look?
items.explain: Look down. A rock below me is the reason to step right.

items.prompt: The whole if is empty. Fill all three.
items.explain: If a rock is to my right, step up. Else, step right.

items.prompt: How many rounds, and what do I look for?
items.explain: 4 rounds, looking right. Right, right, then up, up.

items.prompt: This if looks above me. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Up, up, then the edge is above me, so right and right again: the flower.

items.prompt: This if looks below me. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: A rock below, so right. Then no rock, so down and down again.

items.prompt: A side of an if can hold two steps. Which two?
items.explain: Down, right, then the else carries me on. A side can hold as many steps as it needs.

items.prompt: Follow the else with care. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: A rock, so down. Then no rock, so left, and left is the edge. I stop there.

items.text: A plan that looks can walk a map it has never seen. Same blocks, new rocks. Count the rounds, then let the if decide.

items.prompt: A taller climb. Which way for each side?
items.explain: If a rock is to my right, step up. Else, step right. Same if, taller rocks.

items.prompt: Down these rocks. Which way for each side?
items.explain: If a rock is below me, step right. Else, step down.

items.prompt: Five rounds. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right, down, right, down, right. The count runs out one square before the flower.

items.prompt: Heading left and climbing. Fill all three.
items.explain: If a rock is to my left, step up. Else, step left.

items.prompt: Two ifs inside, one after the other. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Each if takes its own look. Up, up, then right, then the edge above sends me right again.

items.prompt: The if is ready. Count the rounds to the flower.
items.explain: 7 rounds: right, down, right, down, right, down, right.

items.prompt: Six rounds, looking above me. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Up, right, up, up, right, right. This if never turns toward the flower, so I walk straight past it.

items.text: Watch. A repeat can sit inside a repeat. The inside one runs all the way through, every time the outside one goes round once.

items.prompt: The outside repeat is set. How many steps right, each time round?
items.explain: Two steps right and one down, done twice.

items.prompt: The inside is set. How many times round the outside?
items.explain: 3 times round: two right and one down, each time.

items.text: Watch. Three steps inside, two times round: six steps. Inside times outside.

items.prompt: Six squares to the flower, two times round. How many inside?
items.explain: Two rounds of 3 makes 6.

items.prompt: Which step goes in the inner repeat?
items.explain: Right 3 times and one down, done twice.

items.prompt: After the inner repeat, one more step. Which?
items.explain: Down twice, then right, done twice.

items.prompt: Read the inside, then the outside. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two right and one down, two rounds: four along and two down.

items.prompt: Three rounds, with a bump to find. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Up, up, right, then up, up, right. The third round hits the edge at once.

items.text: Look for a pattern inside a pattern. Steps repeat to make a stretch. Stretches repeat to make the whole walk.

items.prompt: Set both counts, the outside first.
items.explain: Outside 3, inside 2: two right and one down, 3 times.

items.prompt: Fill in both steps.
items.explain: Right twice, then down, done twice.

items.prompt: Two repeats inside a repeat. Pick each step.
items.explain: Down twice, right twice, done twice: big stairs.

items.prompt: All empty. Find the stretch, then how often it comes round.
items.explain: Right twice and one down, 3 times. The flower stops me before the last down.

items.prompt: Three down inside, two rounds. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Three down, then right. Next round the first down hits the edge, so I stop there.

items.prompt: This time the plain step comes first. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right, down, down, two rounds: two along and four down.

items.prompt: Two inside two. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two times two is four steps, two short of the flower.

items.prompt: A loop first, then a nest. Set the counts.
items.explain: Down 2 to reach the row, then two right and one up, twice.

items.text: Watch. A long walk from very few blocks. Down, along, up, along, and then all of it again.

items.prompt: Four small repeats in one big one. Pick each step.
items.explain: Down, right, up, right. Twice round reaches the far side.

items.prompt: Two steps at the very middle. Set both counts.
items.explain: 2 inside 2 is four rounds of right and down, which is what the flower needs.

items.prompt: There and back, twice. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Three right, three left, twice. All that walking ends where it began.

items.prompt: An if inside two repeats. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Six looks in all: down, right, right, right, down, down. That reaches the flower.

items.prompt: A snake down the map. Pick each step.
items.explain: Right, down, left, down. The second round's first repeat lands on the flower.

items.prompt: Two repeats inside a repeat. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two right, two down, twice. The flower sits off my path, so I walk on to the last square.

items.prompt: Same stairs, but you set the sizes.
items.explain: Down 2, right 1, twice.

items.text: Watch. Repeat until means no counting. I do the inside, again and again, until the flower. Reaching it ends the run.

items.prompt: No count to set. Which step takes me there?
items.explain: Right, until the flower. It works at any distance.

items.prompt: Which step this time?
items.explain: Down, until the flower.

items.prompt: Two steps inside. No count at all.
items.explain: Right then up, until the flower. Up first runs into a rock.

items.prompt: Three steps inside. Find the piece that comes round.
items.explain: Right, right, up, until the flower.

items.prompt: A count first, then no count. How far down?
items.explain: Down 2 to reach the flower's row, then right until the flower.

items.prompt: A rock on my row. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two steps, then the rock blocks me and the run ends. Until does not get me past a rock.

items.prompt: Follow each round. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right, down, right, down: two rounds and I'm on the flower.

items.prompt: The flower is not on my row. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: I walk right until the edge stops me. Until keeps going, but never changes direction by itself.

items.text: Watch. Until rock means keep going and stop just before it. I look first, every round, so if the rock is already beside me I skip the inside.

items.prompt: Which step until the rock?
items.explain: Right until the rock, then down and right.

items.prompt: What should I go on until?
items.explain: Until a rock is to my right. Until the flower would walk me straight into it.

items.prompt: Two untils in a row. Which step in the second?
items.explain: Right until the edge, then down until the flower.

items.prompt: Look first. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The rock is already beside me, so the inside never runs. Then one step down.

items.prompt: Until a rock, then one step. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Three steps right, stopping beside the rock. Then one step down.

items.prompt: The edge counts when I look. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Down until the edge is below me, then one step right.

items.prompt: Two empty untils. Fill all four gaps.
items.explain: Right until the edge, then down until the flower.

items.prompt: Which step until the rock on this side?
items.explain: Left until the rock, then up and left.

items.text: Watch. Right, left, and I am back on the same square, so nothing will ever change. A loop like that never ends. I follow plans to the letter, but I do stop this one myself.

items.prompt: Round and round. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Down, up, back on the same square: that loop never ends, so I stop it there.

items.prompt: Two steps inside. Choose them so the loop ends.
items.explain: Right, right. Any step that undoes the last one makes a loop that never ends.

items.prompt: A square walk, again and again. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right, down, left, up: back to the start, so the loop never ends and I stop it.

items.prompt: One gap. Choose the step that makes progress.
items.explain: Right then down gets closer every round. Right then left never gets anywhere.

items.prompt: This loop waits for a rock above me. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: No rock above, so up and down again, back on the same square. It never ends, so the last step never runs.

items.prompt: This one does end. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right, up, right, up, and now the edge is above me. I look, and the loop is done.

items.prompt: Two steps inside, three to choose from.
items.explain: Up and right, in either order, get closer every round. Up and down would never end.

items.text: Watch. An if inside a repeat until: no counting at all. This one plan climbs any rocks like these, on any map.

items.prompt: No count now. Which way for each side?
items.explain: If a rock is to my right, step up. Else, step right. Until the flower.

items.prompt: Down these rocks, no count.
items.explain: If a rock is below me, step right. Else, step down. Until the flower.

items.prompt: Rocks both ways. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: A rock to my right, so down, and down is a rock as well. The run ends at the start.

items.prompt: This if sends me backwards. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right, then a rock, so left: back on a square I have looked from. That loop never ends, so I stop it.

items.prompt: Build the if yourself.
items.explain: If a rock is to my left, step up. Else, step left. Until the flower.

items.prompt: Two ifs, each round. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Each if takes its own look: up, up, right, and right again. That lands on the flower.

items.prompt: The biggest climb yet. Same two blocks?
items.explain: Same blocks: if a rock is to my right, step up. Else, step right. The map got bigger and the plan did not.

items.text: Watch. I can learn a new block. New block hop gives a plan a name, and runs nothing by itself. Each hop below it runs the whole plan.

items.prompt: Hop is ready. Fill the gaps.
items.explain: Hop, hop. One name, used twice.

items.prompt: Hop needs its first step. Which one?
items.explain: Right then up. Fix the plan once and both hops use it.

items.prompt: Three hops. Write the plan they all use.
items.explain: Right then up. Three stairs from two tiles.

items.prompt: One hop block. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: One hop is two steps right.

items.prompt: Two hops and a plain step. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two steps, two steps, then one down.

items.prompt: A new block, and nothing that uses it. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: I never move. New block only names the plan: without a hop below it, nothing runs.

items.prompt: Jog is three steps right. Fill the gaps.
items.explain: Jog, then down, down. A block and plain steps mix freely.

items.text: Spot the piece that comes round again. Name it once, then use it as often as you need. Change the plan once, and every use changes with it.

items.prompt: Write stair, then use it.
items.explain: Stair is down then right, used 3 times. Two tiles did the work of six.

items.prompt: Write zig, then use it twice.
items.explain: Zig is two steps right and one down. Used twice, it reaches the flower.

items.prompt: A block inside a repeat. Fill it all.
items.explain: Hop is a step right and a step up, repeated 3 times.

items.prompt: Hop inside a repeat. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two hops are fine. The third starts with a step right and ends with a bump on the bottom edge.

items.prompt: Jog is two steps right. Fill both gaps.
items.explain: Jog, down, jog. Plain steps can sit between uses.

items.prompt: Two new blocks. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Jog, dip, jog: four along and one down.

items.text: Watch. A block can use another block. Each leap is a jog and one step up.

items.prompt: Leap needs its first block.
items.explain: Jog, then up. Blocks built from blocks is how big programs stay small.

items.text: Watch. A block can hold anything: a repeat, an if, a repeat until. Run walks me along until a rock, on any row, however far.

items.prompt: Run goes until a rock. Which step?
items.explain: Right until a rock. It runs a different distance each time it is used.

items.prompt: Run is ready. Use it, with plain steps between.
items.explain: Run, down, run, down, run. Three runs of different lengths, one definition.

items.prompt: Go takes one look and one step. How many times?
items.explain: 7 times: up, right, up, right, up, right, right.

items.prompt: Write go, and the repeat until uses it.
items.explain: If a rock is below me, step right. Else, step down. The until keeps calling go.

items.prompt: Run, down, run. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: One step to the rock, one down, then right to the edge. The edge counts when I look.

items.prompt: A repeat in a block in a repeat. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Jog is two right. Jog then down, two rounds: four along and two down.

items.prompt: Until the flower, using spin. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Spin steps right, then left: back on the same square, so that loop never ends and I stop it.

items.prompt: Set the size of each leap, then how many.
items.explain: Two right and one up, 3 times.

items.text: My own block can have a gap in it. hop(n) says: repeat n times. n stands for whatever number you hand over when you use the block. Watch hop(4).

items.prompt: Hand hop the number that reaches the flower.
items.explain: hop(3) makes n 3, so the repeat inside runs three times.

items.prompt: This hop goes the other way. How far?
items.explain: Five squares, so hop(5). The block stays the same, only the number moves.

items.prompt: hop(2), then one step. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two along from the repeat, then one down. The number decided how far the first part went.

items.text: One block, two uses, two numbers. n is 2 the first time and 1 the next. No second block needed.

items.prompt: Two uses of hop. Each gets its own number.
items.explain: hop(1), a step down, then hop(3). Same block, different lengths.

items.prompt: Now the whole block is a tile. Which hop goes where?
items.explain: hop(2) to reach the gap, then hop(1). Reading the map first tells you both numbers.

items.prompt: Two hops and a step. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Three along, one down, one more along. The flower is on another square, and I go where the blocks say.

items.prompt: The first hop is set. What does the second need?
items.explain: Six squares, two done, so hop(4). Hops add up.

items.text: The gap can go around more than one step. stairs(n) runs two steps, n rounds. More rounds, more stairs.

items.prompt: Inside the block now. Repeat how many times?
items.explain: n: whatever the block was handed. A plain number there would ignore the 4.

items.prompt: Two uses, two numbers. What makes both work?
items.explain: Only n follows what each use hands over: one step, then four.

items.prompt: stairs(2). Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two rounds of along-then-down, so two squares each way.

items.prompt: How many rounds reach the flower?
items.explain: Three squares each way, so stairs(3).

items.prompt: zig(3) is ready. Write the two steps inside.
items.explain: Right then up, three rounds. Up first walks straight into a rock.

items.prompt: Two blocks, each with a number. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: hop(1) is one along. stairs(1) is one more along and one down.

items.prompt: Two tiles, in the order the map needs.
items.explain: stairs(1) slips under the rocks, then hop(2) walks the last row.

items.prompt: A loop around a block. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Each round hops two and steps down one. Two rounds land on the flower.

items.text: A block can hand its number on. twice(n) gives n to hop, two times. So twice(3) walks six squares.

items.prompt: twice(2), then a step. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: twice(2) is hop(2) and hop(2): four along. Then one down.

items.prompt: Six squares away. What does twice need?
items.explain: twice(3): three squares, two times, makes six.

items.prompt: Three rounds. How long is each hop?
items.explain: Six along in three rounds: two each.

items.prompt: Two numbers to find: rounds and length.
items.explain: Three rounds of hop(2). The map has three rows to cross, and that sets the rounds first.

items.prompt: grow uses n in two loops. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: n is 2 for both loops: two along, two down.

items.prompt: grow twice. Pick each size.
items.explain: grow(1) reaches the wide row. grow(2) goes along it and into the gap.

items.prompt: Fill both loops. Mind the rock.
items.explain: Along first, then down. Down first works too: the rock sits inside the corner, clear of both routes.

items.prompt: grow, then hop. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: grow(1) is one each way, and hop(1) is one more along.

items.text: A variable is a number with a name. Set steps to 4 and the name holds 4 until something changes it. Its value shows under the grid. Watch me read it.

items.prompt: Set steps so the loop reaches the flower.
items.explain: Set steps to 3 and the repeat reads 3.

items.prompt: The loop reads steps. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: steps holds 2: two along, then one down.

items.text: Change adds to the value. steps starts at 1, the change adds 2, so it holds 3 when the loop reads it.

items.prompt: It starts at 1. Change it by how much?
items.explain: Four squares away, so 1 plus 3.

items.prompt: Change can take away too. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Change by -1 turns 3 into 2. Two steps, one short of the flower.

items.prompt: One name, read twice. Change it in between.
items.explain: n is 2 for the first loop and 3 for the second, so change it by 1.

items.prompt: Each loop reads a when it gets there. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The first loop reads 1. Then a becomes 3, and the second loop reads 3.

items.prompt: Find the starting value. The rest is fixed.
items.explain: Start at 1: one along and down, then n is 2 for two more along and the last two steps.

items.text: A value can grow while I walk. Each round I add one to steps, then step. Until steps = 4 ends the loop when the count gets there. Watch it climb.

items.prompt: When should the counting loop end?
items.explain: At 2 I stand above the gap. At 3 I walk into the rock.

items.prompt: Follow the count. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The count reaches 2 after two steps, the loop ends, then one down.

items.prompt: The loop counts to 3. Which step goes inside?
items.explain: Down, three times, then the last step along.

items.prompt: The loop ends at 3. Where should the count start?
items.explain: Start at 1 and only two rounds run, which is what this row needs.

items.text: Equals means exactly. Counting by 2 goes 2, 4, 6 and never lands on 3, so that test never holds. Only a rock or the edge stops me.

items.prompt: This one counts by 2. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Round one makes 2, round two makes 4, and the loop ends after two steps.

items.prompt: How much per round gets me to the gap?
items.explain: By 2: two rounds, two steps. By 1 takes four steps and meets the rock.

items.prompt: Two, four... it never equals 3. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The test never holds, so I keep going until the rock stops me.

items.text: Some maps grow several flowers. I pick each one I step on and keep walking until the blocks run out. Then I count what I picked: all of them means the plan worked.

items.prompt: Two flowers. I only stop when the blocks stop.
items.explain: Three steps reach the far flower, and the near one gets picked on the way.

items.prompt: Walk across both. Any route that does it is fine.
items.explain: Along the row and one down, in an order that crosses both flowers.

items.text: Now I want exactly 2 of 3. The look flower asks if I am standing on one, and if so flowers goes up 1. Until flowers = 2 stops me before the third.

items.prompt: Pick exactly 2 of these. When does the loop end?
items.explain: Until flowers = 2. The count ends the walk with the third still growing.

items.prompt: Pick all 3. What should the if look for?
items.explain: Only a flower should add to the count. A rock would never say so here.

items.prompt: Read the count. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Each flower adds one. I stop on the second, with the third still ahead.

items.prompt: Two blocks to place. Which one counts?
items.explain: The step goes first and the count goes inside the if, so it only adds on a flower.

items.prompt: A rock in the way. Which step goes round?
items.explain: A rock to my right sends me down. Two flowers end the loop.

items.text: An if can read a value too. I count rounds in steps, and the round it holds 2, I turn. Same loop, a different move on one round.

items.prompt: On which count should I turn?
items.explain: Count 1: one step along, down past the rock, then along again.

items.prompt: The count starts at 0. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: On count 0 I go down. The other two rounds go along.

items.prompt: Fill both sides of the if.
items.explain: Down on count 1, along on every other round.

items.prompt: How far should steps count this time?
items.explain: Four rounds: along, along, down, along. The count starts at 0.

items.prompt: n grows after each round. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: One along, down, n becomes 2. Two along, down. The steps get longer as n grows.

items.prompt: Each round walks further. What comes after the walk?
items.explain: A step down. The rounds cover 1, 2 and 3 squares along.

items.prompt: Now n shrinks each round. Start at what?
items.explain: Start at 3: three along, then two, then one. The flower is six along.

items.text: > means more than, and < means less than. Until steps > 3 keeps me walking while steps is 3 or under. Watch the count pass 3.

items.prompt: Which sign takes me as far as the gap?
items.explain: Until steps > 1 stops at 2, level with the gap. Equals would stop a square too soon.

items.prompt: Counting back from 5. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: It goes 4, 3, 2: three steps before it is less than 3.

items.prompt: Four steps from 5. Less than what?
items.explain: Four rounds take it to 1, the first value less than 2.

items.prompt: One round along, then down. Which sign?
items.explain: Steps > 0 holds from the second round on, and that one goes down.

items.prompt: Less than 2 means two rounds. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Counts 0 and 1 go along. Count 2 is not less than 2, so it goes down.

items.prompt: A sign and a number this time.
items.explain: Less than 2: two along and then two down.

items.prompt: It only counts upward. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Steps never gets less than 0, so the loop runs until the rock stops me.

items.prompt: Pick exactly 2. More than what ends the walk?
items.explain: More than 1. The count passes 1 as soon as it holds 2.

items.text: Not flips a look. Until not rock below says: keep going while there is a rock below me, and stop at the first open square. Watch me walk the wall.

items.prompt: Not what? Stop me over the gap.
items.explain: Not rock below stops me over the gap. The other look is true at once, so I would never start along the row.

items.prompt: Down until no rock beside me. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The rocks end on the bottom row. There I step along once.

items.prompt: If not rock beside me... fill both sides.
items.explain: No rock: go along. A rock: go down. Not just swaps which side is which.

items.prompt: Read the not carefully. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Rock below me, so along. Then no rock: down, and down again.

items.prompt: Both flowers, with a not inside. How many rounds?
items.explain: Four rounds reach the far flower. The not side is empty, so only a flower adds.

items.prompt: Not less than what stops me on the flower?
items.explain: Not less than 3 means 3 or more, and that is three steps.

items.prompt: Not less than 2. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: n reaches 2 after two steps. That is no longer less than 2, so one down and done.

items.prompt: Two untils. What stops the second one?
items.explain: Not rock below stops me over the gap, ready to step down.

items.text: And wants both looks to hold. Or wants at least one. Until rock beside me or rock below: I stop at the first sign of either.

items.prompt: Stop beside the rock. Which test does it?
items.explain: Or: the rock beside me is enough. And would wait for a rock below as well.

items.text: Now and. Going down needs a rock beside me and a rock or edge above me, both at once. Anywhere else, I step along.

items.prompt: Go down only in a corner. Which test?
items.explain: Both must hold. The open start has nothing beside it, so there it steps along.

items.prompt: Both rocks at once. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Only the far corner has the edge beside me, but no rock below. So I bump off the edge.

items.prompt: Pick 2. Steps is the backup: how high can it go?
items.explain: Six steps is more than the walk needs, so the flower count ends it first.

items.prompt: Whichever comes first. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The rock comes after one step, long before the count gets to 3.

items.prompt: Either look sends me down. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The edge above, then a rock beside me: down, down. Then neither holds, so one along.

items.prompt: And with a not inside. Fill both sides.
items.explain: A rock below with the way along open: step along. Otherwise down.

items.prompt: A not around an or. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Already neither rock is near, so the test holds and I never take a step.

items.text: A list keeps values in order. For each way in the list, I do the blocks inside once, with way holding the next value. Go way steps whichever way it holds.

items.prompt: One value is missing. Which goes there?
items.explain: Three along. A list is only values, in the order they are walked.

items.prompt: Fill the whole list. Any route to the flower is fine.
items.explain: Two up and two along, in any order that stays on the grid.

items.prompt: Read the list from the start. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: One along, two down. The list runs from first to last, and each value is used once.

items.prompt: Two gaps in the middle. Mind the rocks.
items.explain: Along then down, and the last value takes me onto the flower.

items.prompt: The list is ready. What goes inside the loop?
items.explain: go way follows the list. A plain up would ignore it.

items.prompt: Two blocks inside. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Each value runs twice: two along, two down.

items.prompt: Two blocks inside. So what belongs in the list?
items.explain: Each value runs twice, and the flower is two squares each way. Either order works.

items.prompt: A list inside a repeat. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The list runs from the start each round: two along and one down, twice.

items.text: A list can hold numbers too. Each number becomes how far I go, and hop holds it while the blocks inside run. Watch hop change each round.

items.prompt: Which number finishes the walk?
items.explain: Five squares, two done, so 3.

items.prompt: Read each number in turn. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Three along and down, one along and down, then none along and down.

items.prompt: What should the loop inside repeat?
items.explain: hop: the value this round. A fixed 3 would run off the map.

items.prompt: Two numbers to find. Match them to the row lengths.
items.explain: One, then two, then one more. The if only steps down where it can.

items.prompt: The first and last are set. What about the middle?
items.explain: Two along the middle row reaches the next gap.

items.prompt: The list hands each number to hop. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: hop(2), down, hop(1), down. A list and a block work well together.

items.prompt: hop gets one number from the list. How far first?
items.explain: Two along, then down. The 0 means no along at all, and down reaches the flower.

items.prompt: I add up the list before I walk. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Total holds 1, then 3, then 4. So four steps, two short of the flower.

items.text: Blocks inside a list loop can still look. Here a rock beside me sends me down, whatever the list says. Otherwise I follow the next value.

items.prompt: A look comes before each value. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Rock below: along, whatever the list says. Then the list takes over: down, down.

items.prompt: When should I go down instead of following?
items.explain: At a rock beside me. Flower would never turn me, and I would walk straight into it.

items.prompt: All three flowers. What does the gap need?
items.explain: Six along crosses all three. Going back would leave the far one.

items.prompt: The third value meets the edge. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two along. The third round sees the edge and goes down instead.

items.prompt: Which block walks this list?
items.explain: go way. Three along, two down, around the rocks.

items.prompt: Two values, then along. Go round the wall.
items.explain: Down, down, then along the bottom row.

items.prompt: Fill the gap. Mind the rock.
items.explain: Along, along, up, up. Up any sooner meets the rock.

items.prompt: A rock in the way. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The list keeps its order. Right works, then down hits a rock, and the walk ends there.

items.text: New game. Everywhere I stand gets painted. The faint squares are a shape to draw, and I need to cover them and nothing else. No flower this time.

items.prompt: Draw the whole line.
items.explain: Three steps paint three more squares. Four would need a square that is not there.

items.prompt: Finish the corner.
items.explain: Two along and two down. The faint squares are the plan.

items.prompt: Follow the shape as I paint it. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Along, down, then one along. I end on the last faint square.

items.prompt: A small square. Two routes draw it. Take either.
items.explain: Three steps round the square, in either direction. What counts is the squares painted.

items.prompt: Two rows, three wide. What finishes it?
items.explain: Back along the second row. Walking the same way twice would miss squares.

items.text: Extra paint counts too. This walk covers the whole line, then one square too many. Close, and the shape is not the same.

items.prompt: Stop in time. How many steps?
items.explain: Two steps, and every faint square is painted with nothing extra.

items.prompt: A T on its side. One step to go.
items.explain: Back through the middle and on. Walking a square twice costs nothing.

items.text: A square is four sides, and loops are good at sides. One repeat per side, and the shape draws itself.

items.prompt: Same square, smaller. How long is each side?
items.explain: Two on every side. Same number, four times.

items.prompt: Now the sides. In what order do they go?
items.explain: Each side starts where the last one ended, in either direction round the ring.

items.prompt: Three sides. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Along, down, back. The fourth side is still faint.

items.prompt: A staircase. Two steps inside the loop.
items.explain: Along then down, three rounds. Each round is one stair.

items.prompt: A comb. Two loops are missing their step.
items.explain: Down a tooth, along, and back up. Two rounds paint it, and the last tooth comes from the climb.

items.prompt: Follow the comb. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Each round goes down, along and back up, so I finish at the end of the row I started on.

items.prompt: Back and forth, row by row. What finishes it?
items.explain: Along the last row. Painting in rows is how a printer works.

items.prompt: Big stairs. Find the rounds and the width.
items.explain: Two rounds, two along: a loop in a loop draws a bigger staircase.

items.text: A list of ways and one loop inside it: that is a whole square in three blocks. Everything you have built so far can draw.

items.prompt: One way is missing from the list.
items.explain: Down: the turn between the first side and the third.

items.prompt: A bigger square, the same list. How long is a side?
items.explain: Three. One number changed, and the whole shape grew.

items.prompt: Two values, two steps each. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two along, two down: a corner.

items.prompt: A block that draws a line. How long?
items.explain: line(3). Four would walk past the shape, off the edge.

items.prompt: n shrinks each side. Where does it start?
items.explain: Start at 3: three along, two down, one back. A shrinking value makes a spiral.

items.prompt: Follow n as it shrinks. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Three, then two, then one. I end inside the curl.

items.prompt: No counts at all. What stops the first loop?
items.explain: The edge beside me. That works for any width of shape.

items.prompt: Along while the count is low. Less than what?
items.explain: Less than 3: three rounds along, and the other two go down.

items.text: A bug is a block that does the wrong thing. I follow it anyway. Watch where I stop: the bug is on the way there. Then tap that block and pick what goes in its place.

items.prompt: Watch where I stop. Tap the block to change, then pick its fix.
items.explain: The up step hits the edge. A right step there reaches the flower.

items.prompt: I stopped early again. Find the block.
items.explain: Left hits the edge. A right step there gets me to the flower.

items.prompt: So close! Find the block.
items.explain: The last step should be up. Down from there is the edge.

items.prompt: I reach the column of the flower, then stop. Tap the block.
items.explain: The last step should be up, onto the flower.

items.prompt: I never take a step. Which block is at fault?
items.explain: The first step walks into the rock. Down first, then right, right.

items.prompt: Read it before it runs. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Two steps right, then the third hits the edge. Reading ahead is how bugs get caught early.

items.prompt: A longer plan, one bad block.
items.explain: The up in the middle hits a rock. A right step there, and the last up lands on the flower.

items.text: Watch. The count can be the bug. Three steps, and the flower is four away. You can tap a number too.

items.prompt: One count short. Tap the number, then fix it.
items.explain: Six squares away, so 6. Off by one is the most common bug there is.

items.prompt: Which count is off?
items.explain: The first loop stops too early: right 3 times, not 2.

items.prompt: A bad step inside the loop runs every round.
items.explain: Up should be down. Fix one block inside a loop and every round is fixed.

items.prompt: A nest with one wrong number.
items.explain: The outside count should be higher: 3 rounds of two right and one down reach the flower.

items.prompt: An until that bumps. Find the block.
items.explain: Up hits the edge. Right then down gets closer every round.

items.prompt: This loop never ends. Which block undoes the last one?
items.explain: The left undoes the right. Right, right, and the loop ends on the flower.

items.prompt: This until looks the wrong way. Tap what it looks for.
items.explain: It should look right. Looking down, I never see the rock on my row.

items.prompt: Spot the trouble before it runs. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right, up, right, then up hits the edge. So the up in the loop is where a bug would be.

items.text: Watch. An if can look the wrong way. I checked above me when the rock is beside me, so I walked straight into it. You can tap what an if looks for too.

items.prompt: This if looks the wrong way. Fix the look.
items.explain: It should look right. The rocks are beside me, not above me.

items.prompt: This if looks the correct way, then steps the wrong way.
items.explain: A rock to my right should send me up, not down.

items.prompt: One side of this if is wrong. Which one?
items.explain: With no rock below me I should step down. Left only hits the edge.

items.prompt: The bug is inside a block. Both uses have it.
items.explain: Down should be up. One fix inside hop, and both uses are fixed.

items.prompt: A plain step where a block should go.
items.explain: The last step should be jog: one step right stops short of the flower.

items.prompt: A long climb, one bad block.
items.explain: With a rock above me, step right. Left only hits the edge.

items.prompt: Read this one first. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right, then a rock, so up: and up is the edge. The bug would be that up.

items.prompt: A count hiding in a longer plan.
items.explain: Right 2 times, so the up lands on the flower. With 1, the rock is above me.

items.text: Every new block can hold a bug: a value, a sign, a list. Same method as before. Watch the run, tap the block at fault, then pick its replacement.

items.prompt: I walk into the rock. Which block is at fault?
items.explain: The loop should end at 2, level with the gap.

items.prompt: I was handed a 4. Why do I stop short?
items.explain: The repeat ignores n. Repeat n, and the 4 gets used.

items.prompt: This loop never even starts. Tap what is off.
items.explain: Steps is already less than 2. Until steps = 2 walks there first.

items.prompt: One value in the list works against the others.
items.explain: Up undoes the down before it. Right there, and the list ends on the flower.

items.prompt: The list looks fine, and I still bump. Why?
items.explain: The inside ignores the list. go way follows it.

items.prompt: Paint in the wrong place. One side is off.
items.explain: The third side is one too short, so the last side runs up the middle.

items.prompt: This and wants two things. One never comes.
items.explain: There is no rock below me at the gap. Looking above instead, the edge is there.

items.prompt: Pick exactly 2. The count stays at 0.
items.explain: The if looks for rocks. It should look for a flower.

items.prompt: Read it first. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: It starts at 1, so only two rounds run. A start value is a common place for a bug.

items.text: Real programs are written as text. Here is one plan twice: blocks, then JavaScript. Each step is a line, and the semicolon ends it. Same plan, new words.

items.prompt: Only the code now. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: One right, one down, one right: the same three blocks written as words.

items.prompt: Read it from the first line to the last. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Up, up, right. Code runs top to bottom, just as blocks do.

items.prompt: One line is missing. Which goes there?
items.explain: The middle line is right(); and nothing changes but the way it looks.

items.text: A repeat in JavaScript is a for loop. Here i counts the rounds: it starts at 0, and while it is under 3 the lines inside run. Rounds 0, 1, 2: three times.

items.prompt: A step, then a for loop. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: One right, then up 3 times.

items.prompt: Which number makes this loop reach the flower?
items.explain: i < 4 runs rounds 0, 1, 2 and 3: four steps.

items.prompt: Which line goes inside the loop?
items.explain: right(); inside the braces runs 5 times.

items.prompt: Two lines inside the braces. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right and down, two rounds: two along and two down.

items.text: One for inside another. The inner one counts with j, a new name, so the two counters stay apart.

items.prompt: Follow i and j. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: j counts two steps right, then one down, and i does that twice. That lands on the flower.

items.prompt: How many rounds of i?
items.explain: i < 3: three rounds of two right and one down.

items.text: A repeat until is a while loop. The ! means not, so this says: while I am not on the flower, step right. rock("right") asks about a rock the same way.

items.prompt: While there is no rock, step. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Right until a rock is beside me, then the line after the braces: one down.

items.prompt: Which line goes inside this while?
items.explain: right(); runs until flower() is true.

items.prompt: Which test goes after the ! ?
items.explain: rock("right") stops me beside the rock. flower() would walk me into it.

items.prompt: Look at the two lines inside. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: right(); then left(); puts me back on the same square, so that loop never ends and I stop it.

items.prompt: Three inside, two outside. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Three down, one right. Then the next down is the edge, so I stop there.

items.text: An if reads the same in JavaScript. The test goes in brackets, then one set of braces for each side.

items.prompt: One if, one look. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: No rock to my right, so the else side runs: one step right.

items.prompt: Fill the two sides.
items.explain: If a rock is to my right, up. Else, right.

items.prompt: An if inside a for. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Rock, so down. Then no rock, so right, and right again.

items.text: Your own block is a function. The word function gives the plan a name, and hop(); runs it. Same idea, same two parts.

items.prompt: Read the function first, then what runs. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: The function runs nothing by itself. Then hop, hop, down: four along and one down.

items.prompt: Fill the two lines at the bottom.
items.explain: hop(); twice. Calling a function by name is most of what programs do.

items.prompt: Write the two lines inside the function.
items.explain: First right(); and then up(); and three calls run them three times.

items.prompt: A function, an if and a while: all of it together. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: go looks once and steps once, and the while keeps calling it. That reaches the flower, and you can read every line.

items.text: A variable starts with let. After that the name holds the value, and a for loop can read it. Blocks, then JavaScript.

items.prompt: Only the code now. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: steps holds 2, so the for loop runs twice. Then one down.

items.prompt: Which number goes after the = ?
items.explain: let steps = 4; and the loop runs four times.

items.text: Here = means store, not equals. steps = steps + 1 works out the sum, then stores it. And === asks if two things are equal, with the ! asking for the opposite.

items.prompt: Follow n through the while. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: n becomes 1, then 2, with a step each time. Then the line after the braces.

items.prompt: The while keeps going until n equals what?
items.explain: n === 3 stops it after three steps.

items.text: A parameter goes in the brackets of a function, and the number goes in the brackets where you call it. So hop(4) runs with n holding 4.

items.prompt: Two calls, one step between. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: One along, one down, one along.

items.prompt: Fill the number in each call.
items.explain: hop(1); then down(); then hop(3); and the one function does both.

items.text: Tests look nearly the same in code. < and > stay, equals is ===, and is &&, or is ||, and not is !. Each answers true or false.

items.prompt: An if with a <. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: n is 0 and then 1, both less than 2: along twice. Then n is 2: down.

items.prompt: Which sign takes me as far as the gap?
items.explain: While not n > 1: two steps, then I stand above the gap.

items.prompt: Which test turns me at the rock?
items.explain: || only needs one of them, and the rock beside me is enough.

items.prompt: Two ! in one line. Tap where I stop.
items.explain: Not not: while there is a rock beside me, go down. So I stop on the first open square.

items.text: A list in code is an array: values in square brackets, separated by commas. for...of gives me each one in order, and go(way) steps whichever way it holds.

items.prompt: Read the array from the start. Tap where I stop.
